title: NaijaStay
description: A backend API for managing hotel rooms, guests, staff, bookings, availability, and day-to-day hotel operations. Built around the practical problems of a real hotel: room availability, temporary holds, booking conflicts, staff permissions, check-in/check-out workflows, housekeeping states, caching, rate limiting, and migrations.
highlights: 2,814 LOC across domain modules: rooms, bookings, payments, users, auth
4-role RBAC (guest, receptionist, housekeeper, manager) via reusable dependencies
Server-side price calculation — client never trusted for totals
Redis-backed temporary room holds with expiry
Docker Compose with healthcheck gating so the API waits for Postgres and Redis
SSE streaming for room status, APScheduler for background jobs
Middleware-based request logging and SlowAPI rate limiting
problem: A hotel booking system has to do more than store a reservation. When a guest searches for a room, the system must determine whether that room is genuinely available for the requested dates — not just whether an is_available flag is set. If a guest temporarily holds a room while completing a booking, another guest must not be able to take the same room during that period. And hotel employees should not all have the same level of access.
constraints: PostgreSQL is the source of truth; Redis is a performance layer, never the authority
Booking price must be calculated server-side — a client-supplied total is a vulnerability
Four roles with genuinely different permissions, not one role with if-statements
Schema changes must be explicit and reproducible across environments
The API must start only when its dependencies are healthy
architecture: Domain-oriented layout: app/domains/{users,rooms,bookings,payments,auth} each own models, schemas, service, and router
Routers handle HTTP concerns only; business rules live in service layers where they are reusable and independently testable
Reusable role dependencies enforce authorization instead of duplicating permission checks
Redis holds are consumed on booking completion or expire naturally
Alembic migrations manage all schema changes; create_all() is never used in normal operation
Docker Compose orchestrates API + PostgreSQL + Redis with healthchecks and dependency ordering
decisions: Chose pessimistic locking for booking creation — the double-booking window is rare but catastrophic, so correctness beats throughput
Separated booking status from room-cleaning status: a room is not ready just because the previous booking ended
Cached read-heavy endpoints only, with invalidation on room or pricing changes — never cached booking operations
Used SQLModel over raw SQLAlchemy for schema-first models with Pydantic validation, accepting the abstraction cost for development speed
Centralized logging in middleware so routers stay focused on business logic
next: Payment gateway integration (currently a mock provider)
API versioning and a frontend client
